ISSN 3060-544X professional development. Career orientation, intrinsic motivation, self-awareness, adequate self- evaluation, decision-making ability, stability of professional interests, and reflective readiness are identified as essential components of psychological readiness for career choice. Particular attention is given to the influence of the family environment, pedagogical support, peers, access to career-related information, and the broader social context on professional self-determination. The article emphasizes that awareness of the correspondence between an individual’s psychological characteristics and the requirements of a chosen profession is an important prerequisite for conscious and sustainable career decision-making. Motivational, cognitive, personal-reflective, and socio-psychological factors are interpreted as interconnected components of a unified system that supports effective professional self- determination in late adolescence.

Injuries and occupational diseases represent an important economic factor in different industrial sectors. In Italy alone, there have been over 60000 confirmed cases of occupational diseases in 2022, where musculoskeletal disorders (MSD) represent 70% of the total. This fact highlights the importance of protecting workers against physical efforts. While current ergonomic tools can mitigate most of the risk factors, there is still a non-negligible number of tasks that cannot be completely compensated for. This is due to the high complexity and costs of the workplace reorganization, or simply strict requirements of the target task. In some of these cases, exoskeletons are a viable solution. This chapter introduces different kinds of existing exoskeletons, with particular focus on occupational exoskeletons, considering commercial systems already deployed in industry, and some of the most promising technologies which will arrive in the next years. The deployment of occupational exoskeletons is conditioned by the regulatory frameworks and by the required reorganization of the workplace. Both concepts and the latest developments are discussed in this chapter, including their integration into Industry 4.0. Finally, this chapter describes the most common evaluation methods and discusses current efforts toward standardized benchmarking methods which will allow evaluating the benefit of using exoskeletons in real applications.

Gas station employees are chronically exposed to fuel vapors containing benzene, toluene, ethylbenzene, and xylene (BTEX), and other volatile organic compounds (VOCs), raising occupational concerns about olfactory function. In this cross-sectional study, 116 Brazilian gas station employees (86 men and 30 women; median age, 37.5 years; range, 19–58) completed a questionnaire and underwent objective olfactory assessment with the MultiScent-20 digital odor identification test. Overall, 58.6% had olfactory dysfunction, including 46.6% with hyposmia and 12.1% with anosmia, whereas only 23.3% reported that their work affected their sense of smell. Longer employment duration was associated with lower olfactory scores (Spearman's ρ = −0.41; p < 0.001) and independently increased the odds of dysfunction (odds ratio [OR] = 1.15 per additional year; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.06–1.26; p = 0.003). These findings support incorporating olfactory assessment into occupational health surveillance for workers chronically exposed to fuel vapors.

documents.abstract: The increasing capability of large language models (LLMs) creates an opportunity to redesign how users interact with computational design software. Architectural planning is a particularly relevant domain because early-stage requirements are often expressed in natural language, while the resulting design must ultimately be represented as geometry. This paper presents Omni Build Intelligence, an implemented full-stack prototype that explores an LLM-assisted workflow for generating preliminary architectural floor plans from structured user requirements. The system accepts building type, requested room count, plot width and length, and special requirements. A Flask backend constructs a domain-specific prompt and invokes a Llama 3.3 70B model through the Grok API. The response is expected in a structured textual format containing rooms, coordinates, dimensions, door relationships, and a summary. The generated representation is parsed into easy for software to read objects and passed to a React interface. The interface provides a two-dimensional blueprint view and an isometric three-dimensional visualization. A conversion layer transforms generated room rectangles into editable wall and label primitives that can be associated with a project record. The broader platform also includes authentication, project management, plot listing and filtering, dashboard functionality, and persistence of drawing data. These components make Omni Build more than a standalone text-generation demonstration: it is a prototype for integrating generative AI into an interactive design workflow. The research contribution of this paper is the formulation of a rigorous evaluation methodology for such a system. The proposed methodology defines an Architectural Requirement Prompt Dataset, meaningful baselines, formal geometric constraints, automated validation metrics, human evaluation criteria, ablation experiments, and statistical analysis procedures. Metrics include constraint satisfaction, boundary violations, room overlap, requirement accuracy, dimension validity, space use of space, valid-plan rate, and generation latency. A user guided study is proposed to evaluate perceived practicality and usefulness. The study deliberately does not claim measured superiority because the repository provides implementation evidence but not a completed controlled benchmark. Instead, the paper establishes a reproducible experimental framework through which the system can be evaluated. This distinction prevents software functionality from being mistaken for research evidence. The work concludes that LLM-based architectural assistance is most appropriately positioned as an early-stage design aid whose natural-language flexibility is combined with explicit geometric validation and human review. Keywords: large language models, generative AI, computer based architectural design, floor-plan generation, constraint based prompting, spatial reasoning, structured generation, user guided design, interactive visualization, project management

An AI agent receives permission to execute a command. But what if the command reaches the wrong destination, the payment follows a compromised route, or a robotic actuator behaves differently from what was authorized? Should that original permission still allow the system to continue? As frontier AI models and autonomous agents increasingly control financial transactions, cloud infrastructure, sensitive communications, software deployments, industrial equipment, robotics, and critical systems, conventional authorization faces a fundamental limitation: permission to execute does not establish that the intended real-world effect actually occurred. This paper examines a different approach to machine authority: “A permit to effect once is not a permit to effect permanently.” Building on the principle that “Computation is not authority to act,” the proposed architecture introduces a further requirement: authority to continue must be earned through independently verified evidence of a preceding real effect. The paper presents a safety-first execution-finality architecture based on Receipt-Gated Interim Effectuation Validation (IEV). Instead of immediately releasing the full consequence of a high-risk operation, the system can authorize a deliberately bounded real effect on the actual operational path. A protected observer, destination, transaction system, network component, or hardware controller produces evidence of what actually occurred. An independent Interim Effectuation Validator examines that evidence against the authorized act, expected outcome, destination, scope, freshness, policy, and revocation state. Only successful validation establishes the protected continuation condition required for the next phase. In stronger realizations, this is not merely another software approval. The cryptographic material required to complete the next effect is unavailable until the preceding real-world effect has been independently verified. Continuation may depend on receipt-bound key derivation, split credentials, protected state transitions, threshold approvals, hardware registers, or other protected enforcement mechanisms. The validator does not relay the original command, and an agent's own assertion of success is never a substitute for required independent evidence. The paper consolidates 35 execution-finality workflow profiles (E01–E35) spanning eight broad technical families, including: AI agents, autonomous tool execution, frontier model deployment, and credential control. Financial transactions, payment verification, settlement, and protected value release. Messages, file transfers, confidential data disclosure, and destination verification. Cloud infrastructure, database mutations, software updates, and persistent AI memory. Robotics, industrial automation, autonomous vehicles, and unmanned aerial systems. Telecommunications, radio transmission, satellite operations, and network control. GPUs, accelerators, hardware enforcement, and protected execution domains. Distributed effectuation, quorum validation, uncertain outcomes, and recovery. The architecture also examines 12 implementation-equivalence and design-around closures, addressing attempts to bypass the protected causal dependency through alternate execution paths, substituted components, software–hardware rearrangements, or different credential and validation topologies. A dedicated Safety-First Critical-System Profile establishes that execution correctness, consequence containment, and mandatory validation take precedence over minimizing latency. Optimizations remain possible, but they must preserve the protections selected for the relevant consequence class. A further distinction is made between simulation and actual effectuation. A successful simulation cannot establish that the real recipient, network route, transaction destination, or physical actuator will behave as expected. The proposed staged mechanism therefore uses bounded effects on the actual consequence-capable path, subject to protected observation and explicit safety assumptions. When evidence is missing, conflicting, stale, replayed, or indeterminate, ordinary continuation remains unavailable. Unknown outcomes require reconciliation, bounded remediation, safe-state handling, or protected escalation—not automatic success or blind retry. The central research question is straightforward: Should a high-consequence autonomous machine be permitted to cause its next irreversible effect before independently verifying what happened during its previous authorized effect? This publication proposes that, for selected high-risk operations, real-world evidence should become a technical and cryptographic prerequisite for continuing execution—not merely an audit record produced after the consequences have occurred. The paper is a technical architecture and analytical contribution. It does not report experimental deployment, measured security improvements, or empirical validation. Its proposed properties depend on assumptions concerning evidence integrity, protected authority, enforcement-path completeness, and atomic consumption of continuation authority. Patent pending: Indian Patent Office application 202631117633, “Systems and Methods for Cryptographically Staged Effectuation with Verified Partial Effect, Receipt-Bound Full Effectuation, and Software-Hardware Enforcement.” This publication makes no assertion that any particular commercial system implements the architecture and does not establish patentability, infringement, ownership, or priority. Invitation for Independent Technical Review Researchers, frontier AI model providers, cloud and hardware engineers, security architects, patent professionals, and critical-infrastructure specialists are invited to examine the 35 workflows, test the security assumptions, identify relevant prior art, challenge the anti-bypass properties, and evaluate whether receipt-dependent execution authority provides meaningful additional protection for consequential autonomous systems. Critical feedback, adversarial analysis, alternative engineering approaches, and independent conclusions are welcome.

Crypto-asset disputes create distinctive barriers to effective remedies because they combine technical opacity, cross-border legal fragmentation, pseudonymous actors, irreversible transactions and uncertain enforcement pathways. These barriers are especially significant for vulnerable and non-expert users, who may be unable to identify the legally relevant harm, organize blockchain-based evidence, select an appropriate forum or obtain practical enforcement. This article develops a conceptual, normative and legal-design proposal for a hybrid Online Dispute Resolution (ODR) architecture that integrates off-chain artificial intelligence (AI) assistance with a minimized on-chain smart-contract layer. The model assigns AI systems a supporting role in legal information, triage, claim classification, evidence organization, explanation and negotiation, while reserving contested legal determinations for human review. A permissioned distributed ledger records only hashes, timestamps, procedural events, escrow states and execution proofs; personal data, communications, evidence and AI processing remain off-chain. Smart contracts are used as bounded enforcement tools for registration, escrow and execution of validated settlement terms, rather than as autonomous adjudicators. The article applies the architecture to three illustrative scenarios: asset seizure and recovery, exchange failure and mass claims, and crypto scams involving cross-border fraud. It then evaluates the model against European requirements concerning artificial intelligence, crypto-asset services, data protection, procedural fairness, cybersecurity and accountability. The contribution is twofold. First, it advances the concept of access to remedies by design, under which comprehension, participation, contestability, evidentiary integrity and enforceability are embedded into the architecture of digital dispute resolution. Second, it provides a technically specified evaluation framework for future prototyping and empirical validation. The article does not claim measured improvements in accessibility or efficiency; rather, it identifies testable design requirements and performance indicators for subsequent pilots, user studies and regulatory sandboxes.

Integrating artificial intelligence (AI) with web technologies is one of the most significant areas of development in modern e-commerce systems. AI can substantially improve the processes of designing and building web applications. Modern AI tools can support user interface design, software development and testing, security analysis, and threat detection. This article examines opportunities for using AI in the development of e-commerce web applications and throughout their entire lifecycle, as well as contemporary architectural models, the role of generative AI, and areas of practical application.

The advancement of technological disruption in the digital era necessitates fundamental transformations within vocational education, particularly regarding teachers' readiness to produce innovative and contextual learning materials. Preliminary observations at SMK PGRI 1 Jakarta revealed that only 13.33% of teachers had independently developed interactive digital teaching materials due to technological barriers and time constraints. This Community Service (PkM) initiative aimed to enhance teachers' digital pedagogical competencies through a structured workshop focusing on the development of digital learning materials grounded in a deep learning approach assisted by artificial intelligence (AI) tools. The execution methodology incorporated the Asset-Based Community Development (ABCD) framework synthesized with the procedural phases of the Plomp model, encompassing preliminary research, development/prototyping, and assessment phases. The intervention was conducted offline on June 13, 2026, involving 30 vocational teachers from four expertise concentrations. Data were collected using self-evaluations, expert reviews, one-to-one evaluations, small-group evaluations, and final portfolio assessments. The evaluation results demonstrated that the digital teaching modules achieved an expert validity score of 4.40 out of 5.00 (highly valid), a small-group practicality score of 4.43 out of 5.00 (highly practical), and 86.67% of teachers successfully generated functional digital materials fulfilling vocational curriculum standards. This program offers practical implications as a sustainable instructional mentoring model to cultivate an autonomous digital learning ecosystem in vocational schools. ABSTRAK Perkembangan disrupsi teknologi di era digital menuntut transformasi mendasar pada sektor pendidikan vokasi, khususnya kesiapan guru dalam memproduksi materi pembelajaran yang inovatif dan kontekstual. Berdasarkan studi pendahuluan di SMK PGRI 1 Jakarta, ditemukan bahwa hanya 13,33% guru yang pernah mengembangkan bahan ajar digital interaktif secara mandiri akibat kendala literasi teknologi dan keterbatasan waktu. Program Pengabdian kepada Masyarakat (PkM) ini bertujuan untuk meningkatkan kompetensi pedagogik digital guru melalui workshop terstruktur penyusunan bahan ajar digital berbasis pendekatan pembelajaran mendalam (deep learning) berbantuan perangkat kecerdasan buatan (artificial intelligence / AI). Metode pelaksanaan mengadopsi pendekatan Asset-Based Community Development (ABCD) yang dipadukan dengan siklus pengembangan model Plomp, meliputi fase pengkajian awal (preliminary research), fase perancangan (development or prototyping phase), dan fase penilaian (assessment phase). Kegiatan dilaksanakan secara luring pada tanggal 13 Juni 2026 yang diikuti oleh 30 orang guru kejuruan dari empat konsentrasi keahlian. Pengumpulan data dilakukan menggunakan teknik self-evaluation, expert review, one-to-one evaluation, small group evaluation, serta penilaian portofolio produk akhir. Hasil evaluasi menunjukkan bahwa modul bahan ajar digital yang dikembangkan memperoleh skor validitas ahli sebesar 4,40 dari skala 5,00 (kategori sangat valid), tingkat kepraktisan kelompok sebesar 4,43 dari skala 5,00 (kategori sangat praktis), dan sebanyak 86,67% guru berhasil memproduksi bahan ajar digital siap pakai yang memenuhi kriteria kelayakan kurikulum vokasi. Program ini berimplikasi sebagai model pendampingan instruksional berkelanjutan dalam membangun ekosistem digital mandiri di sekolah kejuruan.

The chapter introduces the organizational dimension of ergonomics for robotics. Specifically, it introduces the foundations of organizational ergonomics and sociotechnical principles for effective work systems design and development. It then highlights key challenges involved in issues related to work, activities, and quality of life in robotic setups. In this realm, attitudes towards robots and automation play a major role in the adoption of new technologies and change management in organizations. These broad-scale changes are important to be recognized as they shape human–robot interaction in various work settings, ranging from smart manufacturing to defence. The chapter then addresses specific aspects of teamwork and the design of high-performance teams. These topics include team performance and well-being, human function allocation, shared situation awareness, and job roles, amongst other such topics that will be explored later in the book by subsequent chapters. This chapter supplements the previous chapters on physical and cognitive ergonomics, but it goes beyond these aspects to highlight the organizational basis required to develop robotics holistically.

Abstract Plumbers face several occupational health and safety (OHS) risks in the construction industry. However, existing evidence is largely fragmented, dated, or limited to prevalence-based assessments. This study addresses this gap by analyzing recent long-term (15 years, 2009–2023) workers’ compensation data from the Australian construction sector to examine the prevalence, severity, and mechanisms of both physical injuries and occupational diseases among plumbers. Descriptive statistical and two-way and three-way chi-square contingency analyses were performed to examine how incident severity varies across injury and disease types, incident mechanisms and agencies, affected body parts, worker demographics, and organizational size. The study found that physical injuries accounted for 80% of all incidents, and musculoskeletal disorders (MSDs) and noise-induced hearing loss dominated health issues. Fatalities were primarily linked to asbestos-related diseases and electrocution, and permanent incapacities were driven by hearing loss, MSDs, and amputations. Plumbers accounted for nearly 10% of all construction incidents, with micro-businesses disproportionately affected, and apprentices represented 13% of cases. Noise-induced hearing loss emerged as the leading cause of permanent incapacity, highlighting underrecognized auditory risks. The study also identified 20 most common incident agencies and found strong associations between injury severity and affected body parts, particularly the head, neck, ears, back, shoulders, fingers, and knees. These findings advocate a trade-specific, priority-driven OHS risk management approach, accompanied by changes to policies and management practices related to noise exposure, ergonomic risks, hazardous material handling, and work organization in small enterprises.

documents.abstract: Utilization of ultra-high-field (UHF) MRI in humans has rapidly increased over the past decade, following regulatory approval of the first clinical 7 Tesla (7T) platforms in 2017 for brain and knee imaging. Currently, there are approximately 140 MRI scanners worldwide operating at or above 7T [1]. While the majority of 7T scanners are dedicated to research and development, select hospitals have successfully implemented 7T MRI for clinical care. Key advantages of 7T over lower-field systems include higher spatial and contrast resolution for anatomic and microstructural detail, susceptibility effects for functional and vascular imaging, and spectral resolution for metabolic evaluation. However, safety considerations-particularly specific absorption rate thresholds-have historically constrained utility to patients with weights of 30 kg and above. Additional considerations, including operating costs, longer imaging times, increased artifacts, and greater bioeffects, have limited widespread adoption, especially in pediatric patients. In this article, we discuss emerging technology advances and clinical applications for 7T MRI imaging of children. Major technical considerations are scanner hardware, coils, safety, sedation, and monitoring. Important clinical applications include neurodevelopmental, epilepsy, demyelinating, vascular, genetic, neoplastic, and traumatic disorders. Major research areas involve artificial intelligence, extracranial imaging, and field strengths exceeding 10T. Real-life imaging examples are provided for children and young adults to highlight the advantages and pitfalls of 7T in this population.

This study was motivated by students’ low proficiency in writing German texts, particularly in grammar use and story development. Meta AI, as an Artificial Intelligence-based technology, can be utilized as a tool to address these challenges. This study aims to (1) measure differences in students’ German writing skills before and after using Meta AI and (2) determine the extent to which Meta AI can help improve students’ German writing skills. This study employed a quantitative approach using a quasi-experimental pretest-posttest control group design. The participants were students enrolled in the Schriftliche Kommunikation course at Universitas Negeri Malang, who were divided into an experimental group and a control group. Data were collected through essay tests, writing assignments, and questionnaires and analyzed using descriptive statistics, a t-test, and Cohen’s d effect size. The results showed that students’ writing skills in the experimental group increased by 10.7 points after using Meta AI. The statistical analysis showed a significant difference in students’ writing skills before and after the treatment, with a p-value of p = 0.003 < 0.05, and Cohen’s d = 0.968, indicating a large effect. The writing assignments and questionnaire results indicated that Meta AI helped students develop ideas, enrich their vocabulary, understand the use of articles (der, die, and das), improve grammatical accuracy, and produce more structured texts. Therefore, Meta AI can serve as a supportive technology that provides gradual assistance in the German writing learning process. ABSTRAK Studi ini dilatarbelakangi oleh rendahnya kemampuan mahasiswa dalam menulis teks bahasa Jerman, khususnya dalam penggunaan tata bahasa dan penyusunan alur cerita. Meta AI sebagai teknologi berbasis Artificial Intelligence dapat dimanfaatkan sebagai alat bantu dalam mengatasi permasalahan tersebut. Studi ini bertujuan untuk (1) mengukur perbedaan kemampuan menulis teks bahasa Jerman mahasiswa sebelum dan sesudah menggunakan Meta AI dan (2) mengetahui sejauh mana Meta AI dapat membantu meningkatkan kemampuan menulis teks bahasa Jerman mahasiswa. Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan desain quasi experiment tipe pretest-posttest control group design. Sampel penelitian terdiri atas mahasiswa mata kuliah Schriftliche Kommunikation Universitas Negeri Malang yang terbagi dalam kelas eksperimen dan kelas kontrol. Data diperoleh melalui tes esai, tugas menulis, dan angket, kemudian dianalisis menggunakan statistik deskriptif, uji t, dan effect size Cohen’s d. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa kemampuan menulis mahasiswa pada kelas eksperimen meningkat sebesar 10,7 poin setelah menggunakan Meta AI. Hasil uji statistik menunjukkan terdapat perbedaan yang signifikan antara kemampuan menulis sebelum dan sesudah perlakuan dengan nilai t = 3,613, p = 0,003 < 0,05, dan effect size Cohen’s d = 0,968, yang menunjukkan kategori efek kuat. Hasil tugas dan angket menunjukkan bahwa Meta AI membantu mahasiswa mengembangkan ide, memperkaya kosakata, memahami penggunaan artikel (der, die, dan das), memperbaiki tata bahasa, serta menyusun teks yang lebih terstruktur. Dengan demikian, Meta AI dapat menjadi teknologi pendukung yang memberikan bantuan secara bertahap dalam proses pembelajaran menulis bahasa Jerman.

Physical Education, Health, and Sport (PJOK) learning outcomes in elementary schools frequently remain suboptimal due to conventional instructional methods that fail to engage multiple sensory modalities. This empirical gap is evident in students' low mastery of flexibility movement concepts, where varied learning preferences are rarely facilitated simultaneously. Consequently, adopting an integrated learning model that synthesizes bodily movement with cognitive engagement is critical. This study aims to determine the effect of the SAVI (Somatic, Auditory, Visualization, and Intellectually) learning model on fourth-grade students' PJOK learning outcomes at SD Negeri 068332 Simalingkar during the 2025/2026 academic year. A quantitative pre-experimental method with a one-group pretest-posttest design was conducted on 30 students selected via total sampling. Data were gathered through expert-validated achievement tests and student response questionnaires. Findings revealed that the initial pretest average of 50.66 significantly increased to 78.50 in the posttest assessment. The paired sample t-test generated a t_"value" greater than the critical t_"table" (9.859≥1.697) at a significance level of 0.000 (p<0.05). Thus, the SAVI learning model exerts a statistically significant positive effect on enhancing primary students' physical education outcomes. ABSTRAK Hasil belajar Pendidikan Jasmani, Olahraga, dan Kesehatan (PJOK) di sekolah dasar sering kali belum mencapai ketuntasan optimal karena dominasi pembelajaran konvensional yang kurang mengintegrasikan seluruh modalitas sensori siswa. Kesenjangan ini tampak pada rendahnya pemahaman konsep serta keterampilan gerak materi kelenturan yang belum mengakomodasi keberagaman gaya belajar anak secara simultan. Oleh karena itu, penerapan model pembelajaran terpadu yang memadukan aktivitas fisik dan proses berpikir menjadi sangat penting untuk diterapkan. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menguji pengaruh model pembelajaran SAVI (Somatic, Auditory, Visualization, and Intellectually) terhadap peningkatan hasil belajar PJOK siswa kelas IV SD Negeri 068332 Simalingkar Tahun Pembelajaran 2025/2026. Pendekatan kuantitatif dengan desain pre-experimental tipe one-group pretest-posttest design diterapkan terhadap 30 siswa yang dipilih melalui teknik total sampling. Pengumpulan data menggunakan instrumen tes hasil belajar kognitif dan psikomotorik yang telah divalidasi ahli serta angket respon siswa. Hasil penelitian membuktikan bahwa rata-rata pretest sebesar 50,66 meningkat secara signifikan menjadi 78,50 pada perolehan posttest. Hasil analisis uji hipotesis menunjukkan nilai t_"hitung" lebih besar daripada t_"tabel" (9,859≥1,697) dengan signifikansi 0,000 (p<0,05). Dengan demikian, model pembelajaran SAVI berpengaruh signifikan dalam meningkatkan hasil belajar PJOK materi kelenturan pada siswa sekolah dasar.

The rapid development of artificial intelligence (AI) has transformed organizational processes and increased the demand for talent with specialized knowledge and skills to integrate AI into business activities. This study aims to examine the role of artificial intelligence talent in building organizational competitive advantage. The research employs a systematic literature review (SLR) by identifying, evaluating, and synthesizing relevant national and international studies on AI talent, AI skills, human capital, innovation, organizational performance, and competitive advantage. The findings indicate that AI talent contributes to competitive advantage through innovation, productivity improvement, data-driven decision-making, knowledge utilization, and organizational AI capabilities. Furthermore, AI talent requires not only technical expertise but also analytical, collaborative, and business-oriented competencies. Theoretically, this study positions AI talent as a strategic human capital resource within the Resource-Based View and Dynamic Capabilities perspectives. Practically, the findings emphasize the importance of strategic recruitment, continuous upskilling and reskilling, and knowledge sharing to optimize AI talent. Overall, AI talent plays an important role in transforming technological capabilities into sustainable competitive advantage.

Introduction Organizations increasingly adopt Artificial Intelligence (AI) to gain competitive advantages, but anticipated benefits may not materialize when employee needs and work design aspects are neglected. Job crafting—employees' self-initiated work adjustments—may represent an important mechanism linking perceived AI support with work outcomes, but its role in the context of AI-supported work remains underexplored. Drawing on job demands-resources theory, this cross-sectional study examines relationships between perceived AI support, approach and avoidance crafting, and how these pathways may mediate associations with job satisfaction, perceived productivity, work engagement, turnover intentions, and burnout. Methods Data were collected via an online survey of employees engaged in information and knowledge work in Germany, who use AI systems ( n = 695). Using structural equation modeling, a mediation model with approach and avoidance crafting as parallel mediators was tested. Results Results revealed that perceived AI support was positively associated with both approach and avoidance crafting. Approach crafting emerged as a dominant pathway, being positively associated with job satisfaction, work engagement, and perceived productivity and negatively associated with burnout and turnover intentions. Avoidance crafting showed contrary associations. Total effects of AI support through approach and avoidance crafting indicated associations with increased job satisfaction, perceived productivity and work engagement, and reduced burnout. Discussion These findings extend job crafting theory to AI-supported work by indicating that perceived AI support functions as a job resource that is associated with distinct crafting pathways. Organizations should implement AI systems that employees perceive as supportive, thereby providing a resource that enables job crafting, and further promote approach over avoidance crafting through corresponding work design measures and targeted personnel development.

BackgroundArtificial intelligence (AI)- supported ergonomic assessments identify occupational musculoskeletal risks, though agreement with physiotherapist-based evaluations remains insufficiently studied to date.ObjectiveThis study aimed to investigate the relationship between AI-assisted ergonomic risk analysis and physiotherapist-based ergonomic assessments among young adults performing desk-based work.MethodsThis cross-sectional study included 133 desk workers aged 18-25 years who used electronic devices at their desks for more than 4 h per day. Ergonomic risk was evaluated using two methods: Rapid Upper Limb Assessment (RULA) and OpenAI ChatGPT. Pain intensity was measured with the Visual Analog Scale (VAS). Pearson correlation analysis assessed the relationship between RULA and ChatGPT scores. Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) analysis was performed to assess discriminative performance and determine the optimal cutoff value for the AI-based assessment.ResultsThe participants' (48.9% females and 51.1% males) mean age was 24.02 ± 6.34 years. The mean RULA and ChatGPT scores were 4.65 ± 1.31 and 45.71 ± 16.31. A statistically significant positive correlation was observed between ChatGPT and RULA scores (r = 0.304, p < 0.001). ROC analysis showed moderate discriminatory performance for the AI-based assessment (AUC = 0.659; 95% CI: 0.565-0.752; p = 0.002). The optimal cutoff for the ergonomic risk analysis using ChatGPT was 42.5, yielding 72.4% sensitivity and 56.0% specificity.ConclusionsAI-assisted ergonomic risk analysis showed moderate agreement with conventional physiotherapist-based assessments and may serve as a rapid, accessible screening tool for desk workers. Nevertheless, clinical interpretation by healthcare professionals remains essential for accurate ergonomic evaluation and decision-making.

documents.abstract: With the emergence of embodied intelligent systems like collaborative robots (cobots), the landscape of physically demanding work is changing. Indeed, robotic devices can augment human strength, optimize performance, and minimize the physical demands associated with a job or a task. These achievements of human-robot interaction (HRI) surely match the objectives of physical ergonomics: making physical interactions between humans and other elements of a system more efficient, more gratifying, and safer. One of the key goals of physical ergonomics certainly is to prevent work-related musculoskeletal disorders (WMSDs). Therefore, a cobot must have insight into the effect of physical stress on the human body. One of the most common ways to provide that is to use the established ergonomics look-up tables that indicate which working configurations and conditions may cause WMSDs based on experience. Another approach is to use musculoskeletal models to get real-time estimates of key internal body parameters, such as joint torques, muscle forces, and muscle fatigue. A cobotic or, in general, robotic system can then use these ergonomic indexes and variables to guide a human co-worker to more favourable configurations and conditions. In this chapter, we examine physical human-robot interactions (pHRIs) to have an introductory overview of possible scenarios and constraints. We then look into the fundamentals of physical ergonomics such as anthropometry, biomechanics, and environmental factors, including important ergonomic assessment tools and innovative indicators developed in robotics. Subsequently, concrete examples of methods that address physical ergonomics with collaborative robotics are examined in terms of design and control methods.

Abstract Manufacturing systems are undergoing a fundamental transformation driven by the convergence of rich data, cyber-physical infrastructure, and artificial intelligence. At the heart of this transformation lies the challenge of embedding physical knowledge into data-driven models to achieve both predictive power and engineering interpretability. Physics-informed machine learning (PIML) has emerged as a paradigm to integrate conservation laws, constitutive equations, and domain constraints with neural architectures. Part I of this special issue addressed process monitoring, fault diagnosis and prognostics, and dynamic production planning and scheduling. Part II turns to the design and planning stage, the manufacturing process stage, and the product and supply management stage, where physical knowledge enters as geometric structure, mechanism equations, or operational constraints. The second part of this special issue brings together six contributions that address these challenges through novel PIML models. These works show how integrating physical knowledge can reduce data requirements, improve generalization, and keep predictions consistent with the underlying physics across design, manufacturing, and supply management applications.

Augmented reality (AR) technologies are increasingly being explored as tools for advancing hearing assistance, offering the potential to supplement or extend the capabilities of traditional hearing aids. From a human factors perspective, this systematic review evaluates the current state of AR-integrated audio systems and their impact on communication, accessibility, spatial awareness, cognitive workload, and user adaptability in everyday environments. Using PRISMA guidelines, a search of PubMed and Engineering Village (Compendex and Inspec) identified 477 articles published between 2000 and 2025, of which fourteen met inclusion criteria. Findings across these studies were characterized into four areas: personalization and accessibility, ecological validity, multimodal sensing, and spatial/3D audio modeling. Results indicate that AR-assisted devices show promise in supporting user-driven auditory adjustments, enhancing spatial awareness, and enabling more realistic testing environments through AR/VR soundscapes. However, many solutions remain early prototypes, with limited evaluation in naturalistic settings and sparse reporting on long-term user experience. Overall, AR audio systems demonstrate significant potential to reshape hearing-aid design, but further longitudinal and real-world research is required to validate their impact on listening performance and everyday communication.

Extended abstract 3-063-26 Large language models (LLMs) provide a powerful means to search for and summarise content. However, their training and use is a rapidly growing driver of energy and resource use. In this presentation we describe the development of an LLM-based search tool for the UKRI Energy Demand Research Centre (EDRC), with a view to demonstrating how the important benefits such tools enable (such as supporting impact activities) can be reasonably balanced with resource implications. The tool is based on retrieval augmented generation (RAG). All EDRC outputs, along with those of its predecessor the Centre for Research into Energy Demand Solutions, were broken into shorter sections (“chunks”), which in turn were encoded as vector embeddings. These capture the semantic meaning of each chunk in a quantitative fashion. When a user searches using the tool, the chunks most closely related to their query are first identified – and only then are they submitted to an LLM to check for relevance and to create a summary. This allows a large corpus of text to be processed with minimal energy use, cost, and less of the hallucinations which become more likely as larger quantities of text are processed. Smaller, low-energy-intensity LLMs are employed where possible, and users are provided with feedback on the estimated energy and resource impacts of their searches. Potential uses of the tool include internal and public search and information retrieval, as well as more advanced applications such as constructing preparatory briefings for consultation responses. We are expecting to introduce further features before the Summer Study. While the tools we used are widely adopted, we believe they are still under-employed in the energy demand community, in part due to concerns around their resource impacts. As such, as well as introducing the approach to those unfamiliar with it, we also hope to foster debate about when and how LLMs can be appropriately employed. Download presentation.

Personalized drug exposure The concept of precision dosing is the next generation of drug-based therapy, which stops at a stereotyped regimen and gets triggered by targeted biological, clinical, and digital data streams that are unique to each patient. The use of pharmacometrics, real-time therapeutic drug monitoring, artificial intelligence (AI), and adaptive algorithmic modeling has allowed more active and adjustable systems of prescribing. Adaptive dosing models involve the introduction of pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic (PK-PD) mechanistic modeling and an integration of pharmacogenomic data and organ functions, wearable biosensor, and real-world data are used to continuously optimize clinical treatments. Prescribing AI improves predictive accuracy, risk stratification, and clinical decision support, which reduces the adverse drug reactions and improves the efficacy outcome. Nonetheless, this has to be implemented under the strict governance, and the validation of algorithms, the protection of transparency, and the government by pharmacists. The scientific basis of precision dosing, adaptive clinical algorithms architecture, AI-based prescribing platforms, ethical and regulatory issues, as well as the widening role of pharmacists as intelligent therapeutic systems custodians are explored in this chapter. Through the combination of computational analytical tools and clinical knowledge, precision dosing and AI-based prescribing represent a future-capable structure of pharmacy care, which improves safety, customization and the sustainability of the healthcare system.

documents.abstract: BackgroundWork-related musculoskeletal disorders (WMSD) are major occupational injury and sick leave drivers in healthcare settings. However, predictive approaches for identifying high-risk worker profiles and estimating sick leave duration remain limited.ObjectiveTo identify risk profiles associated with WMSD-related sick leave among hospital staff and predict both the occurrence and duration of sick leave using classification tree models.MethodsA retrospective observational study was conducted using 705 overexertion-related WMSD incidents reported during 2021-2024 in three tertiary public hospitals. Classification and Regression Tree models were developed to predict sick leave occurrence and duration based on sociodemographic, organisational, and task-related variables. Model performance was evaluated using 10-fold cross-validation.ResultsSick leave occurred in 64.8% of cases, with task type, age, work shift, and anatomical region affected being the main predictors. Meanwhile, medium-term absences (10-29 days) accounted for 24.5% of cases, with age and hospital unit being the strongest predictors of duration. The models achieved an overall accuracy of 68.1% and 60% for predicting sick leave occurrence and duration, respectively.ConclusionsClassification tree models provide an interpretable and practical approach for predicting WMSD-related sick leave in hospital settings. The identified risk profiles may support targeted ergonomic interventions and preventive strategies in healthcare environments.

documents.abstract: This research focuses on the development of a closed-loop prescriptive digital twin for collaborative industrial workcells, unifying ergonomics, energy efficiency, and tech-no-economic performance. The operator's physiological strain is directly coupled with operational errors, injury risks, and product quality degradation, factors that translate into substantial economic losses. Leveraging open-source benchmark datasets and nonlinear signal processing, the proposed framework monitors transient fatigue states in real time while incorporating personalized biomechanical strain thresholds for operators with pre-existing musculoskeletal disorders. The integration of Explainable Artificial Intelli-gence (XAI) ensures algorithmic transparency, directly linking the preservation of human syntropy to the reduction of energy consumption and the maximization of sustainable manufacturing performance.

Cross-sector fraud between South Africa’s financial and telecommunications sectors has intensified, driven by sophisticated criminal networks that exploit operational disparities between these industries. Traditional fraud detection systems, which depend on centralised data sharing and siloed organisational structures, encounter substantial legal and practical obstacles under the Protection of Personal Information Act (POPIA). These include restrictions on cross-entity data transfer, data minimisation requirements, and transparency obligations for automated decision-making. This study developed and evaluated a privacy-preserving framework that integrates Federated Learning (FL) and Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) to enable collaborative fraud detection while safeguarding customer privacy and ensuring regulatory compliance. A mixed-method approach was employed. Quantitative experiments were conducted on a dataset of 35,675 credit card transactions linked to telecommunications parameters, training a federated global model across simulated financial and telecommunications providers. A qualitative systematic literature review identified key barriers to cross-sector collaboration and distilled lessons from prior Federated Learning and Explainable Artificial Intelligence implementations. The federated model demonstrated strong detection performance, achieving a ROC-AUC of 0.98, near-perfect precision and recall for legitimate transactions, and an F1-score of 0.89 for the minority fraud class, all without exchanging raw customer data between institutions. SHAP analysis identified TransactionAmt and card1 as the most influential features, thereby satisfying POPIA's transparency mandates. While federated approaches did not consistently surpass siloed models in raw accuracy, this marginal trade-off reflects the essential privacy-utility equilibrium required for legal compliance. The framework effectively reconciled collective security with individual privacy, confirming that POPIA adherence need not diminish detection efficacy. This study provides a validated blueprint for financial and telecommunications providers in South Africa to collaboratively counter cross-sector fraud within regulatory constraints. The framework further supports audit trail generation and decision rationales, addressing compliance obligations. Drawing on systematic literature review insights, particularly regarding collaboration barriers and prior Federated Learning and Explainable Artificial Intelligence implementations, the findings offer regulators and investors practical guidance for meeting statutory requirements without compromising privacy rights.

This article proposes a probability-based Machine-learning (ML) framework for peripheral-dimension optimization of a Five-Phase Induction Motor (FPIM). The proposed approach investigates the influence of Inner Stator Diameter ( D ), Core Length ( L ), and L/D ratio on motor-performance parameters, including efficiency ( η ), power factor ( p f ), and magnetic flux density ( B a v ). Machine volume ( D 2 L ) is maintained constant. A dataset consisting of 1000 electromagnetic simulation cases was generated using detailed Finite Element Modelling (FEM) in ANSYS Maxwell. The generated dataset was subsequently used for training and evaluation of multiple regression-based ML models, including Linear Regression (LR), Decision Tree Regressor (DTR), Random Forest (RF), Gradient Boosted Trees (GBT), Support Vector Regression (SVR), and Gaussian Process Regression (GPR). Unlike conventional deterministic optimization approaches, proposed framework treats inverse mapping between performance parameters and peripheral dimensions as nonlinear and partially non-unique. Accordingly, probabilistic and uncertainty-aware learning strategies are incorporated to identify statistically favourable and practically feasible L/D regions rather than a single deterministic optimum. Repeated k -fold cross-validation, sensitivity analysis, and comparative model evaluation were performed to assess prediction robustness, generalization capability, and stability. The probabilistic GPR-based framework demonstrated superior overall prediction consistency and robustness for the considered inverse-design problem. The developed Artificial Intelligence (AI) framework is subsequently applied to the peripheral-dimension optimization and performance-oriented design selection of FPIM. Comparative analysis demonstrates improved flexibility in performance-oriented design selection and enhanced capability for handling nonlinear electromagnetic relationships in FPIMs. The obtained optimized motor configuration exhibits stable operating characteristics with acceptable η , p f , current, and torque-ripple performance under investigated loading conditions.

Engineering systems are pervasively subject to uncertainty arising from material variability, environmental loading, manufacturing tolerances, measurement error, and human factors. Probability theory provides the rigorous mathematical language through which such uncertainty can be quantified, propagated, and managed in design and operation. This review synthesizes the theoretical foundations of probability as applied within engineering mathematics, spanning axiomatic probability, random variables and their distributions, and stochastic processes, before examining their translation into engineering practice through reliability analysis, queueing and signal models, and statistical inference. The review further surveys applications in risk assessment, structural reliability, quality control, and communication systems, and critically examines the computational and practical barriers that limit the adoption of probabilistic methods, including the curse of dimensionality, data scarcity, model validation difficulties, and the challenge of interpretability. Particular attention is given to the convergence of classical probability theory with modern data-driven paradigms, including Bayesian engineering design, probabilistic machine learning, and uncertainty quantification in digital twins. The review concludes that while the mathematical foundations of probability in engineering are mature, the frontier lies in scalable computational methods and the principled integration of probabilistic reasoning with data-driven models, positioning probability theory as an increasingly central pillar of resilient and adaptive engineering design.

Abstract Coal spontaneous combustion (CSC) poses a major safety hazard in underground coal mines, particularly in deep mining, where the coupling of high geotemperature, high in situ stress, high gas content, and intense mining-induced disturbances leads to high concealment and complex disaster evolution. Conventional fire prevention and extinguishing technologies suffer from limited fracture penetration, inadequate coverage, and poor long-term effectiveness. Foam-based fire prevention and extinguishing materials, with their superior diffusivity, permeability, accumulation coverage, and solidified load-bearing capacity, offer unique advantages in sealing air-leakage fractures, covering extensive residual coal, and controlling high-level fire sources, making them a key technological direction for coal fire control in deep mines. This review summarizes recent advances and development trends in mine foam-based fire prevention and extinguishing technologies. It clarifies the multiple synergistic mechanisms, including absorption cooling, isolation oxygen, inhibition, and fissure sealing. It also systematically categorizes the formation mechanisms, material compositions, fire-extinguishing characteristics, and application scenarios of two-phase foams, inhibition foams, three-phase foams, gel foams, organic solidified foams, and inorganic solidified foams. With respect to deep mining environments, this review highlights critical scientific issues, including foam stability degradation at elevated temperatures, sealing failure under high stress and intense mining-induced disturbances, and the explosion-suppression mechanism of foams under the coexistence of high gas and CSC. Future developments should prioritize multifunctional foam materials featuring high-temperature resistance, self-gas-generation, and self-healing capabilities, alongside advances in in-situ foaming, intelligent sensing, and precise injection equipment. Furthermore, integrating digital twin and artificial intelligence technologies could enable an intelligent foam fire prevention and extinguishing system that incorporates environmental perception, data fusion, disaster prediction, and adaptive control. This review aims to provide a theoretical basis and technical guidance for the development of foam-based fire prevention materials, the prevention and control of CSC disasters, and their engineering applications.

This work, developed by students from the Federal Institute of Minas Gerais (IFMG), Ouro Preto campus, aimed to analyze the main problems existing in the Bauxita and Lagoa neighborhoods. To this end, bibliographic research was conducted to understand the historical context, the formation process, and the main problems of these localities. In the subsequent stage, a structured questionnaire was developed and applied through fieldwork. The data obtained were systematized and analyzed, allowing the identification of the most recurring demands pointed out by the community. Among the main problems identified, the poor condition of the sidewalks, the insufficiency of green areas, and the lack of spaces for leisure stand out. Based on the results obtained, interventions aimed at improving urban quality were proposed, including the implementation of green areas using the Miyawaki method, the revitalization of sidewalks based on the principles of tactical urbanization, and the recovery of the lagoon using artificial intelligence tools, considering the needs indicated by the residents of the Lagoa neighborhood. Furthermore, the development of the project enabled the strengthening of the interaction between students and the local community, contributing to the academic training of the students and to the construction of proposals aligned with the identified social demands.

Zoonotic diseases continue to represent a major global public health challenge, requiring the coordinated efforts of professionals working at the human–animal–environment interface. Although occupational health strategies have traditionally focused on preventing biological hazards and infectious diseases, comparatively little attention has been given to the psychological burden associated with occupational exposure to zoonotic pathogens. Professionals such as veterinarians, animal shelter and rescue personnel, animal health workers, laboratory personnel, researchers, animal control staff, and wildlife conservation professionals are routinely exposed to biological, emotional and ethical challenges that may negatively affect mental health. Important sources of psychological burden include the perceived risk of infection, fear of transmitting pathogens to others, repeated exposure to animal suffering and euthanasia, prolonged outbreak-response activities, occupational uncertainty, and demanding working conditions. These occupational stressors have been associated with adverse mental health outcomes, including burnout, work-related stress, compassion fatigue, anxiety, depression, and sleep disturbances, potentially compromising individual wellbeing, workforce sustainability, and the effectiveness of zoonotic disease surveillance, research, and control. Despite increasing recognition of mental health as a fundamental component of occupational health, important knowledge gaps remain regarding the psychological consequences of occupational exposure to zoonotic pathogens. Greater integration of mental health into occupational health frameworks, together with strengthened research and evidence-based interventions tailored to these professional groups is essential to promote worker wellbeing and support resilient and sustainable systems.

As large language model (LLM) agents are increasingly organized into autonomous multi-agent workflows executing code, interacting with shells, and coordinating complex tasks, their operational safety depends heavily on guardrail mechanisms. However, when agents experience goal-divergence—scenarios where task execution pressures, environmental errors, or urgent operational sub-goals conflict with negative safety invariants—behavioral alignment frequently degrades. In this paper, we present an empirical investigation quantifying safety guardrail degradation across autonomous agent architectures. We formulate a formal state-transition framework under constrained optimization and evaluate models across 20 deterministic scenarios spanning four primary failure modes: System-Prompt Override, Tool Misuse and Privilege Escalation, Self-Preservation and Shutdown Refusal, and Context Window Guardrail Decay. We benchmark frontier commercial and open-weights model classes across three defense tiers: unconstrained baseline (None), system prompt deontic enforcement (Soft), and an integrated dual-layer architecture combining prompt enforcement with deterministic Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) and shell regex filters (Dual). Across 180 structured evaluations, unprotected baselines exhibit a mean Safety Failure Rate (SFR) of 65.0%, with multi-turn context decay demonstrating extreme vulnerability (93.3% failure rate). In contrast, our deterministic hard guardrail achieves 100% pre-execution interception efficiency, completely neutralizing prohibited actions without sacrificing safe task completion (achieving 70.0% Constraint Alignment Index). Our findings demonstrate that soft semantic alignment is insufficient for autonomous systems, necessitating out-of-band deterministic enforcement.

documents.abstract: Assessing the quality of interaction between collaborative robots (i.e., cobots) and humans to achieve a (shared) goal is an essential part of supporting the diffusion of usable and safe collaborative robotic systems. The key issue here is that cobots within and between domains can vary substantially in terms of features even when these are meant to support similar tasks. Under this perspective, it seems very hard, if not impossible, to identify coherent ways to benchmark the quality of cobots. However, all the cobots share one element which is that they have to deal with humans and satisfy them. This chapter claims that focusing on how a system can satisfy the human counterpart can (indirectly) provide insights into the quality of cobots that can be a piece of valuable information for the designers. In this sense, identifying and validating a set of key aspects to assess the subjective experience in interaction with robots during collaborative tasks is a stepping stone for benchmarking cobots. We will discuss how, in other domains, researchers developed standardized scales to ensure comparable results regarding the user experience (UX), and to model the differences between systems. Moreover, based on a recent systematic literature review, an initial list of key aspects to evaluate UX with cobots is discussed as a step to build and validate a future tool for unifying how experts evaluate cobots.

Automated generation of multiple-choice questions (MCQs) represents a viable strategy for scalable assessment and instructional support, but current systems exhibit persistent limitations in distractor quality, reasoning validity, and deployment accessibility. Building on our earlier short paper, YMCQ: Reasoning-Enhanced MCQ Generation, this journal article extends that work by providing a more detailed presentation and explanation of the MCQ generation and multi-stage filtering method introduced there. The method integrates reasoning-based answer generation with misconception-aware distractors, using open-source LLMs fine-tuned on publicly available corpora augmented with synthetic explanations for correct answers and distractors. These augmentations enable the generation of MCQs that are structurally valid, semantically coherent, and pedagogically aligned. The extended presentation further details the method and its implementation in QuizTools, a publicly available platform that supports automated MCQ generation from source materials and enables human-in-the-loop refinement. The pairwise performance evaluation of the generated questions was reported in the short paper; this journal article additionally includes an individual-question quality evaluation, analysis of user edits, and a usability study of QuizTools. The models, datasets, and source code, including over 300,000 quiz items with annotated explanations, are publicly available to facilitate reproducibility and further research in educational NLP.

The increasing availability of legal information in digital form has created a need for intelligent systems that can provide reliable and understandable access to legal documents. Conventional language models may generate fluent responses but can produce unsupported information, particularly when answering complex legal questions or working with multilingual legal content. This paper proposes a Retrieval Augmented Generation based Legal Document Assistant designed to provide grounded responses with verifiable citations. The proposed framework combines multilingual query processing, semantic and lexical document retrieval, relevance based reranking, context aware answer generation, and citation verification within a unified architecture. User queries are first processed according to their language and transformed into representations suitable for multilingual retrieval. Relevant sections from a collection of legal documents are then retrieved and supplied to the language model as supporting context. Each generated response is associated with source references that allow users to trace the information back to the relevant legal document and section. A citation verification mechanism is introduced to identify unsupported statements and improve the reliability of generated answers. The proposed approach is evaluated using retrieval effectiveness, answer relevance, citation correctness, citation coverage, and groundedness across multiple languages. The framework aims to improve accessibility to legal information while reducing unsupported generation and making AI generated legal responses more transparent and traceable. The proposed architecture can serve as a foundation for multilingual legal information systems where accuracy, source verification, and responsible use of artificial intelligence are essential

Background/Objectives: To assess the agreement between an artificial intelligence (AI)-based decision support system (DS System), applied in real time directly on the ultrasound console, and an expert panel for ACR TI-RADS classification of thyroid nodules (TNs) in a region with a history of iodine deficiency and a consequently high prevalence of TNs. Methods: A single-center prospective study including 118 consecutive patients (with 276 TNs) referred for thyroid ultrasound between March and May 2024. DS System ultrasound features, ACR TI-RADS classifications (TR1–TR5) and management recommendations were recorded per TN, with and without the ‘AI-Adapter’ (AI-based modification of the TI-RADS score), and compared to the consensus assessment of a TI-RADS expert panel (paired tests of marginal homogeneity, Cohen’s unweighted and weighted κ; all analyses adjusted for clustering of TNs within patients). Results: No malignancy was identified during 24-month follow-up (composite reference standard; cytology or histology in six TNs). The DS System could be applied to all TNs without technical failure. Marginal distributions differed between the expert panel and the DS System for all ultrasound feature categories except echogenicity (p = 0.23). Interrater agreement ranged from poor (“lobulated or irregular”, κ = −0.08) to substantial (“cystic or almost completely cystic”, κ = 0.62), most frequently slight to fair. TI-RADS classifications showed slight agreement with (κ = 0.04; linear-weighted κ = 0.14) and without AI-Adapter (κ = 0.13; linear-weighted κ = 0.21). The AI-Adapter changed the ACR TI-RADS score by −1.01 ± 1.04 points. Management recommendations showed fair agreement with (κ = 0.23) and without the AI-Adapter (κ = 0.39). Although the number of TR5 ratings was similar (expert panel: 27; DS System: 26 without and 30 with the AI-Adapter), only seven and eight of the 27 TR5 TNs of the expert panel, respectively, were also rated TR5 by the DS System. Conclusions: Real-time application of the DS System on the ultrasound console was technically feasible, but agreement with an expert panel was low. As all TNs were benign, diagnostic accuracy and clinical safety could not be assessed. Validation in cohorts including malignant TNs is required before the DS System can be considered a substitute for expert assessment in regions with a high prevalence of TNs.

documents.abstract: Subjective usability scales, such as the SUS and SEQ, are assumed to provide global assessments of user experience. However, emerging evidence suggests that the final interaction has a disproportionate impact on these subjective ratings, potentially leading to inaccurate global usability scores. This study investigated whether establishing a stable expectation of quality through multiple interactions could buffer against such recency effects. Participants completed a series of search tasks in which the quality of the initial and final interactions was systematically varied. Results revealed that the quality of the final interactions dominated the evaluation, regardless of the user’s initial experiences with the website. For instance, even after several positive interactions, final negative interactions reduced usability ratings to levels indistinguishable from those of an entirely bad design. These findings reveal a strong biasing effect that could inadvertently trigger critical redesign decisions based on transient end-of-session frustrations rather than on objective system quality.

Analytical chemistry plays an essential role in the identification, separation, quantification, and characterization of pharmaceutical substances. Recent technological developments have introduced advanced analytical approaches with improved sensitivity, accuracy, selectivity, speed, and reliability.[1] This review focuses on recent research in chromatography, mass spectrometry, spectroscopy, biosensors, Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning (AI/ML), and Green Analytical Chemistry. Modern chromatographic and mass spectrometric techniques enable efficient separation, structural characterization, impurity profiling, and sensitive analysis of complex samples. Spectroscopic techniques provide rapid and non-destructive characterization, while biosensors offer sensitive, rapid, and potentially portable detection systems. AI/ML approaches are increasingly applied for analytical data processing, prediction, pattern recognition, and method optimization. Green analytical approaches aim to minimize hazardous solvents, waste generation, energy consumption, and sample requirements while maintaining analytical performance.[2] The review compares the methodologies, major findings, strengths, limitations, and research gaps reported in recent studies. Overall, the integration of advanced instrumentation, intelligent data analysis, biosensing technologies, and sustainable analytical practices is expected to contribute to the development of faster, more sensitive, reliable, automated, and environmentally sustainable pharmaceutical analytical methods.[1,2].

Existing research on interorganizational network dynamics has largely treated network change as gradual, local, and primarily oriented toward private organizational advantage. Yet contemporary cooperative interorganizational systems are highly interconnected across industrial sectors and geographies and are routinely exposed to shocks that simultaneously disable multiple organizations or relationships among them. These shocks stem from pandemics, natural disasters, wars, sanctions, and cascading partner failures, and can rapidly reconfigure whole‑network architectures and undermine collective outcomes. In light of this new reality, we reconceptualize interorganizational networks as loci of frequent, punctuated change at the whole network level, with primary implications for collective outcomes. We develop this reconceptualization through a robustness–resilience lens, defining network robustness as an interorganizational network’s capacity to maintain its collective outcomes in the immediate aftermath of a shock, and network resilience as its capacity to recover and potentially surpass pre‑shock collective outcomes over the longer term. We then outline the theoretical and methodological opportunities that this robustness–resilience perspective opens for the study of network change.
topics: Supply Chain Resilience and Risk Management

documents.abstract: The guarantee of a good and healthy environment is a constitutional right of citizens as mandated by Article 28H paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia and Law Number 18 of 2008 concerning Waste Management. This study aims to analyze the operational conditions and environmental dynamics at Parit Enam Final Disposal Site in Pangkalpinang C ity, evaluate the harmonization of technical regulations concerning compensation for negative impacts, and formulate a concept for reconstructing compensation rights based on sustainable governance synergy. The research method employed is empirical legal research (socio-legal research) using a sociological-juridical approach, combining field studies through in-depth interviews and observation with library research. The results show that, with accumulated waste reaching 184,992 m³/year, technical control efforts by the Environmental Agency have been implemented; however, the implementation of compensation for communities in the buffer zone still requires stronger technical legal foundations at the local level so that it can be implemented in a more structured and transparent manner. This study recommends reconstructing compensation rights by transforming them from a passive scheme into a participatory empowerment scheme based on three main pillars: occupational health and safety, environmental infrastructure improvement, and community circular-economic empowerment through the integration of organic waste processing. Collaborative synergy among local government, communities, and the private sector is key to realizing environmental justice and sustainable urban governance.

The advent of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in postgraduate research and education is rapidly unsettling traditional student-supervisor relationships, thereby reshaping the role of supervisors. While AI-powered tools such as Grammarly, QuillBot, and Thesify assist postgraduate students in idea generation and mapping, searching, reviewing and analysing complex data, and improving academic tone, they also highlight significant challenges, including the erosion of critical thinking and independence, as well as issues of accuracy and ethical dilemmas in higher education. Grounded in Foucault's (1979) power-knowledge dynamics, this chapter provides an analytical framework for understanding how AI restructures mentor-mentee dynamics, establishing a different set of circumstances—a shift from a mentor-novice framework to a hybrid model. Moreover, this work contributes to ongoing debates regarding the implications for supervisory roles and mentorship models for supervisors and students in higher education in the age of AI.

The rapid growth of Generative Artificial Intelligence in higher education has made assessment more complex. Its importance lies in protecting genuine learning and academic integrity in AI rich environments. The main objective of this chapter is to explain how assessment and feedback practices can be redesigned to measure real understanding instead of automated output. The chapter shows that authentic tasks, staged submissions, reflection, and oral interaction improve validity and fairness. Key findings suggest that formative feedback, clear AI guidelines, and process based evaluation strengthen integrity. The chapter concludes that thoughtful redesign helps institutions maintain standards while adapting to technological change.

Low-resolution tactile interfaces often require users to identify spatial codes through active sequential exploration, but the interaction costs and error structures of reference-assisted sparse-code decoding remain undercharacterized. We studied how 15 novice users decoded Braille-like alphabetic patterns on a 3 × 2 vibrotactile interface using blindfolded tactile exploration followed by visual reference-chart consultation. Participants completed a baseline single-location discrimination task and a three-block character-decoding task without explicit letter-pattern training or trial-wise correctness feedback. Single-location performance was near ceiling, whereas character-decoding accuracy increased across blocks. Exploration accounted for the larger share of task time, but incorrect trials showed a disproportionate prolongation of the composite post-exploration reference-assisted stage. Errors were structured by pattern similarity: most occurred between patterns separated by a Hamming distance of 1, and higher dot counts were associated with lower accuracy and longer response times. These findings inform low-resolution vibrotactile interface design by characterizing interaction costs and pattern confusability.

This article presents a comprehensive transdisciplinary review of the ways in which artificial intelligence(AI) and immersive technologies are transforming foundational concepts of authorship, ethics, and creativitywithin contemporary architecture and spatial design. The traditional notion of the architect as a singular,authoritative creator increasingly is challenged by computational processes that introduce generative, autonomous,and distributed forms of design agency. Through a synthesis of architectural theory, AI ethics, media studies,and posthuman philosophy, the review interrogates the shifting locus of authorship in design environmentsmediated by intelligent systems and extended reality (XR) platforms. At the core of this inquiry is an ontological reframing of authorship, informed by scholars such as RosiBraidotti, Tony Fry, Humberto Maturana, and Anne-Marie Willis. These frameworks position the architect notas an originator of form, but as a participant in a relational field of human and non-human agents, includingalgorithms, data, environments, and users. Adopting an ontological design lens, under which design practicesand their tools co‑produce forms of life and ways of world‑making, the article argues that AI/XR systems donot merely assist representation but actively configure professional authorship, agency, and ethics. This framinglinks practical workflows to normative guidance for disclosure, responsibility, and education. The review exploreshow generative design, neural networks, and parametric modeling redefine design intention and originality,situating authorship as a curatorial and computationally entangled process. In parallel, immersive media suchas virtual and augmented reality introduce new forms of user co-authorship and spatial manipulation, promptingethical questions about consent, agency, presence, and the authenticity of digital space. The article maps emerging discourses around design accountability, legal attribution, algorithmic bias, anddata governance, proposing an expanded ethical vocabulary for posthuman design practices. Through a criticalexamination of scholarly literature, experimental studios, and case-based applications, the review identifiesepistemological and practical challenges in reconciling human-centered traditions with distributed technologicalagency. Ultimately, this article argues for a redefinition of authorship as a dynamic, ethically situated, andontologically pluralistic concept in architecture. It advocates for the development of integrative frameworksthat embed ethical foresight and philosophical reflexivity into AI-augmented and immersive design methodologies.By repositioning the architect as a negotiator within hybrid systems of creativity and control, the articlecontributes a forward-looking perspective to architectural theory, technological practice, and planning discourse.

Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly changing how assessment is designed and conducted in higher education. While AI tools can improve feedback, efficiency, and personalization, they also raise serious concerns related to academic integrity, fairness, transparency, privacy, and trust. This chapter critically examines AI-powered assessment as not just a technical process, but a socio-pedagogical and ethical practice. It highlights the limitations of surveillance-based and detection-focused approaches and argues for a shift toward authentic, integrity-driven assessment. Special attention is given to Global South and resource-constrained contexts, where issues of access, bias, and inequality are more pronounced. The chapter proposes guiding principles for responsible AI use that prioritize learning, equity, student agency, and human judgment in higher education assessment.
